newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan militia says recaptured southern town - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sudan militia says recaptured southern town - paper.

text.p: A militia leader allied with the Sudanese government said his forces have recaptured a town in southern Sudan from rebels, a newspaper reported on Friday.

Southern Sudan Defence Force (SSDF) commander Riek Machar said his forces fought the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) led by John Garang and seized Ayod, about 840 km (500 miles) south of Khartoum, the independent Akhbar al-Youm said.

"The SSDF managed to win in the battle and take control of Ayod...from the forces of rebel Garang," the paper quoted Machar as saying. "Garang's forces launched a fierce attack in the area in the last three days." He added that SSDF forces chased Garang's forces south.
The SSDF is a unified force of factions which signed in April a peace pact with the Islamist Khartoum government.

An SPLA spokesman in Eritrea said on Monday the SPLA took Ayod on the Jonglei Canal 360 km (220 miles) north of Juba on Sunday and Tindilo garrison 120 km (75 miles) northwest of the southern capital.
For 14 years the government has been fighting the SPLA, which wants greater autonomy or independence for the mostly Christian and animist south from the Moslem Arabised north.
